headline: NEVER 🕯️ EVER 🕯️ Forget 9/11's 25th ANNIVERSARY 🇺🇸
text:
TWENTY FIVE 🕰️ years after the 9/11 attacks ✈️ America is marking the solemn 🪦 anniversary with presidents past and present gathering to remember the nearly THREE THOUSAND 💀 lives lost when hijacked planes 🛫 slammed into the World Trade Center 🏙️ the Pentagon 🏛️ and a field in Pennsylvania 🌾. President Donald Trump 🗣️ led the Pentagon ceremony 🪖 while Vice President JD Vance attended the memorial at the World Trade Center site 🏙️ alongside all four living former presidents 👔 and first ladies 👠. Moments of silence 🤫 marked the exact timings of the attacks ⏰ and the names of the victims were read aloud 📢 for nearly four hours ⏳.

GEORGE W BUSH 🧔 who was president during the attacks joined Joe Biden 🕴️ Barack Obama 👔 and Bill Clinton at the World Trade Center memorial 🕯️ where two beams of light 🔦 illuminated the Manhattan sky 🌃 for the Tribute in Light tribute. At the Pentagon ceremony President Trump spoke 📢 renewing the sacred oath 🗝️ we swore a quarter century ago saying quote we will never ever forget 🪦 that's why we fight today ⚔️. He linked the war on terror 🛡️ that followed with his current stance on Iran 🇮🇷 declaring the Islamic Republic will never ever have a nuclear weapon ☢️.

JANICE BROOKS 👩‍💼 had just moved to New York weeks before and was working on the 84th floor of the South Tower when the first plane hit the North Tower ✈️ causing her to evacuate 🏃‍♀️ only for the second plane to strike with an almighty thud 🛬. She heard horror film screams 😱 as debris hit a woman and saw the big gaping hole 🕳️ where her office once stood. Every year bells 🛎️ ring at the exact times the four planes crashed and the Twin Towers fell 🏗️ followed by moments of silence 🤫 this year a seventh bell honored the thousands more who died from related diseases including cancer 🦠 which health officials say claimed more than threefold the nearly 3000 initial lives lost.

A 9/11 widow Terry Strada 👰‍♀️ criticized Saudi Arabia 🇸🇦 and US officials for failing to deliver justice 📜 saying you are missed more each year that passes but how can it be 25 years and still no justice for the role Saudi Arabia played in your murder 🪦. Her comments as national chairperson of 9/11 Families United drew loud applause 👏 from the audience at the Manhattan ceremony. The majority of the 9/11 attackers were from Saudi Arabia with planning led by Osama bin Laden but the 9/11 Commission found no evidence the Saudi government funded al Qaeda directly.

COMMEMORATIONS 🕯️ spread worldwide with events at Buckingham Palace 🏰 in London attended by Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and the US ambassador. In Gander Newfoundland the US ambassador praised the town for taking in thousands of passengers from 38 diverted planes ✈️ saying when people in America hear Gander our hearts soften ❤️. Former Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chrétien added a message for American friends never mistake our generosity for weakness 💪 receiving a standing ovation. In Milan Italian and US firefighters in full gear 🧑‍🚒 climbed 110 floors up and down the Galfa Tower to honor the fallen responders who died climbing the Twin Towers.

US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick lost his brother Gary and colleagues in the attacks while families gathered at the Wall of Names memorial in Pennsylvania to honor the victims of Flight 93 after passengers fought back against the hijackers ✊. The agony endures for the bereaved with many saying the loss is constantly on their mind 🧠 and the quest to identify remains from Ground Zero continues. Spies strategies and missed opportunities mean the lessons of 9/11 are still being learned 📖 even 25 years later as America renews its vow to never ever forget 🕯️.
